purpose: Machine-readable seed lessons distilled from audited mathematical research conversations.
claim_boundary: Examples identify recurring reasoning risks; they do not adjudicate the final mathematical status of any named project.

lessons.trigger_pattern: A local, bounded, finite-volume, truncated, or model-specific theorem is described as the full target theorem.
lessons.kill_test: Compare every quantifier, object class, limit, and regularity assumption in the evidence with the theorem contract.
lessons.repair: Create a separate local theorem node and an explicit bridge node for every omitted limit or universality step.
examples: bounded Wilson-network reconstruction versus full Yang-Mills existence
an infinite gluing family versus every tree
local repair exclusion versus a global no-three-in-line construction

lessons.trigger_pattern: Finite enumeration or numerical agreement is used to carry a universal quantifier.
lessons.kill_test: Construct a perturbation that vanishes on the tested range and differs immediately outside it.
lessons.repair: Add induction, compactness, finite-basis, classification, or another explicit local-to-global theorem.

lessons.trigger_pattern: The manuscript says 'standard', 'therefore', or 'technical details remain' at a load-bearing transition.
lessons.kill_test: Turn the transition into a standalone quantified claim and attempt to state all inputs and outputs.
lessons.repair: Insert the missing claim into the DAG and block all descendants until it is proved.
examples: corner equation after a quotient lifting

lessons.trigger_pattern: Weak and strict definitions, or historical and current definitions, are mixed during a proof.
lessons.kill_test: Version every definition and locate the first proof line using a property absent from the stated version.
lessons.repair: Create a new claim under the stronger definition or prove the missing implication.
examples: initial versus strictly initial Lie subgroup

lessons.trigger_pattern: Operators, products, limits, or derivatives are composed without a common domain and topology contract.
lessons.kill_test: Write the domain, codomain, topology, and regularity beside every arrow in the critical formula.
lessons.repair: Restrict domains, change target spaces, or prove continuity/closability before composition.
examples: L2 differentiation landing in a dual space

lessons.trigger_pattern: Symmetry, monotonicity, linearity, smoothness, or uniformity appears in the proof but not in the theorem statement.
lessons.kill_test: Remove one property at a time and search the smallest counterexample.
lessons.repair: Expose the property as an assumption or replace the proof mechanism.
examples: symmetric star layers used for arbitrary components
linearity omitted from a transport theorem

lessons.trigger_pattern: The certificate generator and verifier share code, normalization, or assumptions.
lessons.kill_test: Tamper with labels, hashes, edges, signs, ranks, and parameters; then rederive from the raw instance with a second implementation.
lessons.repair: Assign distinct independence groups and require two groups for critical claims.

lessons.trigger_pattern: Novelty or open status is inferred from memory, abstracts, or a secondary source.
lessons.kill_test: Inspect the primary source version, exact problem number, definition, and cited prior art.
lessons.repair: Store source claims as evidence with version, section, quotation range, and access date.
examples: historical age of an open problem
definition used by a current monograph

lessons.trigger_pattern: Multiple agents produce routes with different prose but the same invariant and proof calculus.
lessons.kill_test: Normalize mechanism signatures and ask what outcome distinguishes one route from another.
lessons.repair: Merge duplicates and open a route with a genuinely different obstruction, representation, or formalism.

lessons.trigger_pattern: A weighted proof-progress percentage is interpreted as success probability or completed theorem status.
lessons.kill_test: Check target_logical_closure and the list of open critical obligations.
lessons.repair: Display release state and metric semantics beside every percentage.

lessons.trigger_pattern: A sophisticated structure is added because it is suggestive, without closing a proof obligation.
lessons.kill_test: Delete the structure and identify the exact proof line that becomes impossible.
lessons.repair: Keep it exploratory until it yields a typed construction, invariant, obstruction, or falsifiable consequence.
examples: category/topos language without a needed universal property
Hopf structure unrelated to the main convolution application
quantum-group UV intuition without reconstruction bridges

lessons.trigger_pattern: A broad problem can be compressed to one exact obstruction or finite certificate contract.
lessons.kill_test: Verify that solving the compressed object really reconnects to every parent edge in the DAG.
lessons.repair: Promote the compression as a standalone theorem and retain the reconnecting bridge as an explicit obligation.
